# Tasks: Autonomous Review Escalation Precedence

Three canonical units implement the approved Feature 014 definition contract at `.dude/specs/014-autonomous-review-escalation-precedence/spec.md`. This is a prose-contract correction across the coordinator's prompt surfaces plus their existing exact-string pins. No runtime module changes, no stop is reclassified, and no lane, board, command, persistent store, or stop reason is introduced.

Every task that edits `src/` also rebuilds `.github/` with `node scripts/build-dev.mjs` inside that same unit, so each task leaves the tree in a verifiable state. Plan section 6 governs: the rebuild is part of the change set, never a follow-up task. A `src/`-only edit is inert at runtime, and the contract suite's generated-core guard short-circuits only on full `src/` to `.github/` byte parity, so an unrebuilt edit makes that task's own gate unsatisfiable.

No task carries `[P]`. T001 and T002 both write `src/skills/dude-reviewer-protocol/SKILL.md`, `scripts/current-format-contract.test.mjs`, and the regenerated `.github/` projection, so no write sets are genuinely disjoint. Every task traces to a plan phase and a spec requirement.

Durable suffixes are the fixed lowercase hexadecimal encodings of `defr`, `scop`, and `vrfy`.

`src/skills/dude-work/SKILL.md` and every runtime module, including `src/skills/dude-work/recovery.mjs`, are out of scope and must not be edited. Governance's own use of "disposition" for the affected target's lane disposition must survive byte-unchanged. The rebuild projects the whole tree, so an unchanged source yields an unchanged projection: `.github/skills/dude-work/**` must show no diff. Execution may read but must not write any `.dude/specs/014-autonomous-review-escalation-precedence/**` artifact. Line numbers in the plan are prior-session observations and must be re-resolved by content before editing. A required normative change stops with `contract-mismatch: redefine-required`.
